papers.title: TurboVec: A Case Study in Cost-Efficient Private Retrieval for Enterprise RAG via Codebook-Oblivious Quantization

summary.tldr: TurboVec introduces a codebook-oblivious scalar quantizer, TurboQuant, for enterprise RAG, achieving higher recall than trained PQ at lower memory and mitigating data leakage in multi-tenant deployments.
key_points: TurboQuant 4-bit outperforms trained FAISS Product Quantization by 8.5-8.9 percentage points in Recall@5 on DBpedia OpenAI embeddings (100K-999K vectors) at the same memory budget.
TurboQuant offers higher recall than IVF-PQ without training, using 4-8x less memory than HNSW.
TurboVec achieves 11ms median query latency at 100K vectors on Snowpark Container Services, compared to 707ms for warehouse brute-force scan.
Kernel-level allowlist filtering maintains 0.86-0.93 Recall@10 across 10-1000 tenant workloads, significantly outperforming post-filter baselines (0.09-0.19).
Codebook-oblivious design reduces membership inference accuracy to near-random (50.0%) from 57.3% for PQ codebooks, addressing data leakage.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach provides a more cost-efficient and private vector retrieval solution for enterprise RAG systems, improving performance and security in multi-tenant environments.

papers.title: Training Continuous Chain of Thought Models: A Tale of Two Regimes

summary.tldr: C-MTP introduces a direct supervision method for Continuous Chain-of-Thought models, averaging embeddings of CoT traces, outperforming prior direct methods and revealing limitations of current continuous CoT on complex tasks.
key_points: C-MTP directly supervises continuous latent representations by modeling each latent as an average of embeddings from CoT traces.
C-MTP outperforms a prior direct supervision method that approximates the distribution of compressed tokens.
C-MTP performs competitively with slower indirect supervision approaches on simplified CoT traces (<100 tokens).
Both direct and indirect supervision methods for Continuous CoT show a roughly 65% performance drop on complex tasks with longer reasoning traces (>= few hundreds tokens).
summary.why_it_matters: Current continuous CoT methods, regardless of supervision approach, are limited in handling complex tasks requiring longer reasoning traces.

papers.title: Lomekwi: Resource-Bounded Tool Discovery in LLM Agents

summary.tldr: This work introduces a framework to decompose tool discovery in LLM agents into curiosity, recognition, and efficiency, demonstrating inverse scaling of recognition with model size in combinatorial games and real-world-emulating environments.
key_points: Tool discovery is decomposed into curiosity (part discovery), recognition (process discovery), and efficiency (tool use after creation).
The proposed framework can be applied to existing discovery tasks like Voyager.
Recognition inversely scales with model size, evidenced by combinatorial games and a separate real-world-emulating environment.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding the components of tool discovery and the inverse scaling of recognition with model size can inform the development of more efficient and capable LLM agents.

papers.title: CADENCE: Closing the Reasoning Gap via Coverage-Adaptive On-Policy Distillation

summary.tldr: CADENCE is a unified framework for on-policy knowledge distillation, addressing cold-start collapse, state-agnostic divergence scheduling, and binary reward sparsity with targeted mechanisms.
key_points: CADENCE employs DRIFT, a mechanism scheduling per-token convex mixtures of forward-KL and reverse-KL surrogate objectives on student-sampled trajectories.
It includes COVA for coverage-adaptive beta scheduling, FTB for concentrating gradient at high-entropy positions, and CCD for numerical-proximity partial credit.
CADENCE achieved 69.8 ± 0.5% pass@1 on GSM8K for a 0.5B student distilled from a 1.5B teacher, closing 63.2% of the teacher gap.
With a 3B teacher, the 0.5B student reached 72.1 ± 0.4% on GSM8K, closing 76.2% of the teacher gap, outperforming baselines by +4.4 ± 0.7 points.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables strong reasoning quality from distilled models without requiring datacenter-scale hardware, making advanced AI more accessible.

papers.title: Environment-free Synthetic Data Generation for API-Calling Agents

summary.tldr: A novel environment-free method uses LLMs as digital world models to generate synthetic API-calling agent trajectories, overcoming data collection bottlenecks.
key_points: The method generates diverse tasks solvable with provided API specifications using an LLM.
A teacher agent iteratively solves tasks while an LLM simulator generates synthetic API responses conditioned on task context and simulation history.
An LLM judge filters generated trajectories to ensure dataset quality.
The approach was evaluated on AppWorld and OfficeBench, showing significant performance gains for fine-tuned models.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach provides a scalable solution for training API-calling agents across various API ecosystems without requiring fully implemented environments.

papers.title: Trace-Based On-Policy Distillation for Masked Diffusion Language Models

summary.tldr: TOPD is a teacher-supervised framework for diffusion LLMs that distills reasoning ability by supervising a dLLM on its own denoising trajectory using a Reverse-KL objective.
key_points: TOPD samples on-policy diffusion trajectories from the target dLLM.
Teacher token distributions are obtained from a teacher model on corresponding partially denoised states.
The target dLLM is updated with a token-level Reverse Kullback-Leibler objective.
TOPD enabled SDAR-4B-Chat to match TraDo-4B-Instruct's MATH500 accuracy, with +5.7 static and +4.5 dynamic evaluation gains.
TOPD achieved results with 4x fewer rollout rounds, yielding an estimated 96.0x to-accuracy model-compute speedup compared to RL-trained counterparts.
summary.why_it_matters: This method offers a more efficient way to post-train diffusion LLMs for reasoning tasks, reducing computational cost and reliance on sparse rewards.

papers.title: Beyond Semantic Equivalence: Logical Graphs for LLM Uncertainty Quantification

summary.tldr: A new framework, Logical Graph Uncertainty (LGU), models implication and incompatibility among LLM answers to improve uncertainty quantification beyond semantic equivalence, reducing overestimation and false positives.
key_points: LGU explicitly models logical relationships (implication, incompatibility) between distinct LLM answers, unlike semantic entropy which focuses on semantic equivalence.
The framework aggregates probability mass along entailment chains and computes entropy over logically maximal hypotheses.
LGU penalizes mutual incompatibility among hypotheses to refine uncertainty estimation.
On question-answering benchmarks, LGU improved uncertainty estimation, outperforming semantic entropy by up to +7.1% AUROC and +3.5% AUARC.
summary.why_it_matters: Improved uncertainty quantification for LLMs is crucial for their reliable deployment in safety-sensitive applications by reducing false flagging of hallucinations.

papers.title: Beyond Memory Leaderboards: Evaluating Scientific Memory as Budgeted Context Restoration

summary.tldr: New benchmarks (PAIM, PTr) evaluate LLM scientific memory as budgeted context restoration from full papers, revealing that retrieval budget, modality, and evaluation protocols significantly impact performance beyond architectural leaderboards.
key_points: Introduced two full-text scientific-memory benchmarks: Public AI Memory (PAIM; 81 papers, 66 questions) and Public Transformers (PTr; 252 papers, 98 questions).
Evaluated eight memory/retrieval systems, including Theoria, demonstrating that retrieval budget (e.g., Graphiti's 2.6M characters per query) significantly affects leaderboard positions.
Sparse-dense hybrid retrieval (BM25 + dense) was the most significant intervention on PTr, with hybrid variants of Simple RAG, Mem0, and Theoria tying for the lead within 0.03 points.
LLM-as-a-judge rankings showed consistency across frontier judges and agreement with human evaluation, achieving an effective resolution of approximately one point on a ten-point scale.
summary.why_it_matters: This work provides standardized datasets and evaluation protocols to assess scientific memory in LLMs more accurately, emphasizing budgeted, modality-aware context restoration over unconstrained architectural comparisons.

papers.title: Similarity All The Way Up: Multilingual Generalization in LLMs Relies on Language-Level Similarity Structures

summary.tldr: LLMs' latent representations recover the hierarchical structure of the Indo-European language family tree, and this language-level similarity correlates with multilingual generalization performance on XNLI.
key_points: LLMs' latent representations largely recover the hierarchical similarity structure of the Indo-European language family tree.
Languages within the same subfamily are grouped closely together in the LLM's representation space.
The degree to which models reflect this language similarity structure correlates with their performance on the XNLI multilingual natural language inference benchmark.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding how LLMs represent language similarity can inform the development of models with improved multilingual generalization capabilities.

papers.title: Constraint-Anchored Reasoning Traces

summary.tldr: CART is a neuro-symbolic framework that trains MLLMs to interleave natural language reasoning with symbolic constraint assertions, reducing error snowballing by continuous verification and backtracking.
key_points: CART trains MLLMs to interleave natural language reasoning steps with symbolic constraint assertions (e.g., count(red_objects) = 3).
A Constraint Propagation Module, combining a neural grounding head and Boolean Constraint Propagation, continuously verifies anchors against visual features and checks logical consistency.
Upon contradiction, a backtrack controller halts generation and reverts to the last consistent checkpoint, preventing error propagation.
A variable-frequency emission mechanism allows adaptive control of anchor density to avoid trace bloat.
Fine-tuning open-source MLLMs (LLaVA-NeXT, Qwen2-VL) with 218K GQA, CLEVR-CoGenT, and VCR instances, CART reduces snowball rate from 0.65 to 0.14 and improves GQA accuracy by +4.6 percentage points.
summary.why_it_matters: This method significantly improves the reliability and accuracy of MLLM reasoning by mitigating error propagation with minimal inference overhead.

papers.title: RECON: Benchmarking Agent Memory for Compositional Reasoning over Long Contexts

summary.tldr: RECON is a new benchmark for evaluating LLM agent memory for compositional reasoning over long contexts (50k-100k tokens) across criminal, medical, and financial domains, testing six memory-intensive tasks.
key_points: RECON includes 24 case files, each 50k to 100k tokens long, across criminal, medical, and financial domains.

The benchmark evaluates six memory-intensive tasks: reconstructing multi-hop evidence chains, propagating cascading invalidations, resolving source conflicts, counterfactual reasoning, satisfying temporal constraints, and temporal fact retrieval.
Unlike previous benchmarks, RECON assesses the impact of fact changes, tracing affected conclusions, independent support, and alternative timelines.
Current architectures achieve a maximum accuracy of 22.4% on RECON, indicating significant limitations in retrieval and reasoning.
summary.why_it_matters: The low accuracy of current LLM agents on RECON highlights critical deficiencies in their ability to perform reliable compositional reasoning over long, complex contexts, impacting their utility in real-world applications.

papers.title: Falsification-Based Verification of LLM-Generated Optimization Models: Sound Test Batteries and Their Detection Limits

summary.tldr: This paper introduces a falsification-based verification theory for LLM-generated optimization models, using sound test batteries derived from duality and comparative statics.
key_points: The verification method tests candidate models via solver calls on slot-transformed instances, without requiring a reference model or label.
Test classes cover directions, curvature, crush probes, prohibitive limits, annihilation, and exchange, derived from duality, comparative statics, and polyhedral limit arguments.
Every test is sound, ensuring a 0.0% false-positive rate, and a violation certifies unfaithfulness.

Experiments on 326 ground-truth models and four benchmark families show the battery achieves a 0.0% false-positive rate (compared to 54.9% for threshold testers) and detects 70.0% of certified conditional-class mutants.
summary.why_it_matters: This method provides a reliable way to detect errors in LLM-generated optimization models, improving their trustworthiness and practical applicability.

papers.title: OpenLanguageModel: Readable and Composable Small-Language-Model Pretraining for Education and Research

summary.tldr: OpenLanguageModel (OLM) is a PyTorch library for readable, composable small language model pretraining, supporting educational and research applications from notebooks to multi-GPU runs.
key_points: OLM uses ordinary modules with Block, Residual, Repeat, and Parallel components to define model architectures, enabling direct translation from diagrams to code.
The library integrates tokenizers, local/streaming datasets, optimization, mixed precision, callbacks, checkpoints, and hardware-aware execution for CPU, single-GPU, and multi-GPU setups.
Validation demonstrates 90.6% four-GPU weak-scaling efficiency for a 348M-parameter workload and close agreement with independent reference implementations.
OLM includes 27 presets across nine model families and documentation covering LM fundamentals to architecture research.
summary.why_it_matters: OLM simplifies the development, pretraining, and architectural modification of small language models, making advanced research and educational exploration more accessible.

papers.title: Synchronization-Free Algebraic Fingerprints for Large Language Models: From Autoregressive to Diffusion Models

summary.tldr: A novel synchronization-free watermarking scheme for LLMs uses binary congruences from neighboring token pairs, embedding watermark bits via Reed-Solomon polynomial evaluation parity, offering robustness to editing.
key_points: Watermark consists of a single binary congruence generated from a pair of neighboring tokens.
A cryptographic hash determines a Reed-Solomon polynomial evaluation point for each token pair, with parity determining the watermark bit.
The method is resistant to insertions, deletions, and token reordering due to self-contained, local token pair dependency.
Watermark corruption is modeled as a Binary Symmetric Channel, with reliable recovery requiring small redundancy even at high corruption rates.
summary.why_it_matters: This method provides a flexible, synchronization-free watermarking framework for LLMs, enabling reliable attribution of generated text despite modifications.

papers.title: Scalable Causal Imitation Learning

summary.tldr: New off-policy causal imitation learning algorithms, Causal SQIL and Causal IQ-Learn, combine causal adjustment with inverse reinforcement learning objectives to address limitations of prior CIL methods in continuous control tasks.
key_points: Existing Causal Behavioral Cloning (Causal BC) and Causal Generative Adversarial Imitation Learning (Causal GAIL) methods perform poorly in long-horizon, high-dimensional continuous control due to compounding errors, instability, and sample inefficiency.
Causal SQIL and Causal IQ-Learn are off-policy causal imitation learning algorithms that integrate causal adjustment with state-of-the-art inverse reinforcement learning objectives.
These new algorithms operate on causally-adjusted state representations derived from an efficient approximation of the sequential π-backdoor criterion.
The full-horizon adjustment is reduced to a fixed-size sliding window by exploiting the causal structure of continuous control environments.
summary.why_it_matters: This enables effective imitation learning in complex, real-world continuous control scenarios where expert demonstrations are confounded and observations are mismatched.

papers.title: Counterfactual Shapley Credit Assignment

summary.tldr: Counterfactual Shapley Credit Assignment introduces a causal framework using Counterfactual Shapley Values ($\phi$-values) to attribute credit and blame in RL, improving temporal credit assignment in sparse, stochastic, and delayed reward environments.
key_points: Introduces Counterfactual Shapley Credit Assignment, a novel framework grounded in causal theory for credit assignment in RL.
Utilizes Counterfactual Shapley Values ($\phi$-values) to redistribute environmental rewards, enhancing temporal credit assignment.
Addresses challenges of sparse causality, high stochasticity, and delayed rewards while preserving the optimal policy.
Derives a consistent estimator for efficient computation of $\phi$-values.
Enables a new class of policy gradient methods, $\phi$-PPO, combined with Prioritized Trajectory Replay (PTR).
summary.why_it_matters: This framework provides a principled method to isolate true causal drivers of outcomes from spurious correlations and environmental randomness, leading to more efficient and explainable RL agents.

papers.title: Expected Free Energy as Belief-Dependent Utility for rho-POMDPs

summary.tldr: Minimizing Expected Free Energy (EFE) is shown to be equivalent to solving a rho-POMDP with expected information gain as utility, eliminating the need for manual tuning of exploration weights.
key_points: EFE minimization is equivalent to solving a rho-POMDP where the utility is expected information gain and the exploration weight is fixed at w=1.
This equivalence is proven for observe-then-commit POMDPs and extended to factored observation POMDPs, which include interleaved observe-act problems.
Experiments on environments like the Tiger problem, RockSample, and a Structural Inspection benchmark (65,000+ states) show the untuned EFE approach matches or outperforms reward-only planning.
EFE avoids over-exploration common with manually tuned bonuses and positions near the reward-maximizing knee of the success-reward Pareto frontier.
summary.why_it_matters: This provides an out-of-the-box exploration objective for applications like fault detection and medical screening, where information gathering has costs and missed faults have consequences.

papers.title: A Method for Learning Value Systems in Generative AI

summary.tldr: This work adapts a value system learning method for generative AI, simultaneously learning value groundings via a multi-objective reward model and a weighted linear scalarization from pairwise prompt-response preference data.
key_points: The method learns a multi-objective reward model as an implementation of value groundings.
It learns a value system representation as a weighted linear scalarization of the grounding model.
The algorithm dynamically prioritizes grounding learning to ensure coherent value representations.
Evaluation against baselines and a contemporary method uses prompt-response preference datasets.
summary.why_it_matters: This method improves the explainability of value alignment in generative AI by providing explicit computational representations of human value systems.

papers.title: Do Speech Tokens Leak Voiceprints? Speaker Inversion Attacks Against End-to-End Speech Language Models

summary.tldr: This paper investigates speaker inversion attacks against end-to-end speech language models, demonstrating that speech tokens can leak voiceprints, achieving high cosine similarities with only three seconds of output.
key_points: The study formulates the risk of voiceprint leakage from speech tokens as a speaker inversion attack.
A trainable model, Audio BERT (AuB), is introduced to construct token embeddings and aggregate them into speaker-sensitive representations.
SpInv, a two-stage inversion method built on AuB, recovers embeddings in an attacker-specified speaker encoder space.
Evaluations on Moshi, Higgs3, Kimi-Audio, and Qwen3-Omni using VoxCeleb show SpInv achieves cosine similarities above 0.70 with only three seconds of frontend output.
summary.why_it_matters: The findings indicate a significant privacy risk in end-to-end speech language models, as speech tokens can be exploited to recover sensitive speaker characteristics.

papers.title: Principled Direction-Free Intrinsic Motivation through Model-Free Epistemic Free-Energy Estimators

summary.tldr: This paper proposes a novel intrinsic motivation reward based on parameter information gain, maximizing explainable surprise to drive exploration in unsupervised reinforcement learning without precommitting to surprise direction.
key_points: The proposed intrinsic reward is derived from the novelty contribution of a preference-free Expected Free Energy objective, expressed in reward-maximization form.

The intrinsic signal, parameter information gain, is defined as the expected surprise of the next state minus its irreducible part, driving exploration in unresolved dynamics and vanishing in resolved regions.
A pseudocount provides epistemic value, a probe-based penalty captures aleatoric variance, and a short-horizon gate protects informative successors.
A window-based freeze of reward-defining objects ensures a stationary Bellman operator, explicit learning target bounds, and a conditional uniform-concentration result for nonparametric estimators.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach offers a principled, direction-free intrinsic motivation for unsupervised reinforcement learning, enabling effective exploration across diverse environments without issues like irreducible noise or non-stationarity.

papers.title: AgentBrew: Lifelong Knowledge Brewing from Strong Teachers to Weak LLM Agents

summary.tldr: AgentBrew distills interactive experience from strong teachers into external memory for weaker LLM agents, enabling knowledge transfer without weight updates, expert demonstrations, or test-time teacher access.
key_points: AgentBrew uses a failure-triggered teacher (Ralph Loop) to convert student failures into environment-validated notes, addressing sparse feedback.
Student-aware synthesis calibrates teacher knowledge to the weaker student's operational granularity, providing actionable, model-specific guidance.
The method operates without weight updates, expert demonstrations, ground-truth labels, or requiring test-time teacher access.
Evaluations show effectiveness across coding, math, and tool-use tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach allows for the deployment of capable yet compact LLM agents by leveraging stronger teachers during training without increasing test-time computational burden.

papers.title: First-Order Predictable but Pairwise Fragile: Local Task Adaptation in Trained Transformers

summary.tldr: This study finds that while individual perturbations in trained transformers are first-order predictable, pairwise task composition and update ordering are fragile, with order sensitivity appearing within the predictable window.
key_points: Individual perturbations exhibit first-order predictability for loss changes, with effects essentially projecting onto the gradient, across a shared validity window up to scale 10^-2.
Pairwise structure is fragile; two-update order sensitivity appears strictly inside the 10^-2 window for over a third of (model, task pair) combinations.
Task-gradient subspaces rotate within tens of steps, and additivity fails at full task-vector scale on several models.
The Lie bracket H_B g_A - H_A g_B is the leading order-dependent term for sequential task-gradient steps, with its normalized prediction tracking the measured defect at a median ratio of 1.002.
The onset scale eta^dagger for order sensitivity spans three orders of magnitude across models and task pairs.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding the fragility of pairwise task composition and update ordering is crucial for developing more robust and predictable local adaptation methods in large language models.

papers.title: JOR-Bench: Japanese Operations Research Benchmarks for Large Language Models

summary.tldr: JOR-Bench introduces five Japanese-language benchmarks for evaluating LLMs on operations research problems, comprising 1,319 problems translated from existing English benchmarks, covering various OR problem types.
key_points: JOR-Bench consists of five Japanese-translated benchmarks: IndustryOR, MAMO Complex LP, NL4OPT, OptiBench, and OptMATH, totaling 1,319 problems.
The benchmarks cover linear programming, mixed-integer programming, non-linear programming, and combinatorial optimization, providing Japanese problem statements and numerical answers.
Evaluation of seven LLMs showed a -0.3 pp average accuracy difference between English and Japanese versions for strong multilingual models, indicating language-neutral OR formulation ability.
Error analysis revealed cross-lingual differences, including models outputting decision-variable values instead of objective values in Japanese prompts due to pragmatic disambiguation failure.
summary.why_it_matters: JOR-Bench enables standardized, solver-independent evaluation of LLMs' operations research capabilities in Japanese, facilitating cross-lingual performance comparisons and identifying language-specific model limitations.

papers.title: RELIC: Revealed Principles for Learning Interpretable Composable Skills in Multi-Agent Planning

summary.tldr: RELIC is a framework for multi-agent planning that learns interpretable, composable programmatic skills as textual principles, enabling knowledge transfer and reuse across agents with heterogeneous interfaces and private implementations.
key_points: RELIC distills useful decision logic and coordination patterns into compact textual principles, rather than requiring direct program exchange.
These principles can be re-instantiated under agent-specific interfaces and reused across incompatible implementation spaces.
A shared principle memory accumulates transferable knowledge and promotes abstractions that repeatedly improve team-level performance.
The framework supports strategic transfer across both heterogeneous-role and shared-role cooperative teams, preserving local executable implementations and decentralized execution.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach allows agents to improve specialized decision-making skills and coordinate effectively without sharing private executable implementations or relying on common skill representations.

papers.title: A Causal Markov Condition for Value

summary.tldr: This paper introduces the value Causal Markov Condition (v-CMC) to establish a causal value theory, linking causality and utility through a probability-value duality.
key_points: The v-CMC is formulated in local, global, and decomposition versions, and their equivalence is proven.
v-separation is defined and shown to be sound and complete for conditional value independence.
A Bellman-type recursion is derived as a special case of the v-CMC, generalizing standard Bellman recursion to causal DAGs.
The v-CMC supports modular transfer and updating of utility information across causal contexts.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework enables algorithms for causally structured utility elicitation and canonical influence-diagram construction.
